77478.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1113

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Friday! Today, we’re diving into Anthropic's historic $2 trillion IPO, which would be the largest listing ever (we can finally price it thanks to a leaked Coatue deck, why the multiple isn't the scary part here & one number that decides whether $2T truly holds + bonus deep dives into The New Enterprise AI Go-To-Market Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/25a12f7d-d15b-4bbe-b4cd-1e9468a99df2?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & The Age of the One-Person Company [ https://substack.com/redirect/25a7ec68-b47f-42ee-a237-f39ddf0d79ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and Tempo Earn, Stripe's new stablecoin yield play that pays up to 4% a year after Congress banned exactly that (how the GENIUS Act workaround actually works, why Deel's 1.5M contractors are the perfect first customers, & what’s next + bonus dives into Stripe [ https://substack.com/redirect/98cd1fd9-3976-456b-8b52-b9531b55c250?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & the ultimate list of stables resources [ https://substack.com/redirect/dcefa016-57de-4f24-b7f7-82775863a36a?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s just jump straight into the market-changing stuff 🌶️
Anthropic’s historic $2 trillion IPO hands Coatue its 2030 exit four years early 🤯💸
Following the money 💸 Six Anthropic [ https://substack.com/redirect/5d2e6495-3f1d-46cf-ad55-31becff9df11?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] backers told the Financial Times this week that they expect the Claude maker to go public in October 2026 at a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would make it the largest IPO in history, ahead of SpaceX’s $1.77 trillion June debut [ https://substack.com/redirect/05e0eff8-9ea4-4078-b763-b9109c7ae356?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ].
A leaked Coatue [ https://substack.com/redirect/723d5e76-1cbd-48e1-bbf7-5defe8ab8513?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] deck, built on December 2025 company data, shows exactly what one of Anthropic’s most aggressive investors privately underwrote to get in.
The fund’s entry price is in there. So is its modeled 2030 exit, and so is the 35% IRR that October’s rumored offer would hand back four years ahead of schedule. Not bad at all… 👀
Let’s take a closer look at this and unpack Coatue’s math in detail, the one number in the deck that I think decides whether $2 trillion truly holds, and the price where I’d buy. Hint: that price is a lot lower...

77476.subject: It Starts With What They're Building
77476.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/it-starts-with-what-theyre-building

The session was supposed to be over.
One hundred and sixty students, a university lecture hall, a slot on AI agents and Avalanche, the kind of format where you expect a third of the room to drift out early and the rest to stay out of politeness. We had reached the end of what we had prepared. We thanked them.
Nobody moved.
Then the questions started, and they did not stop for another two hours.
That afternoon confirmed something I had been circling for a while: the barrier between people and Web3 was never really technical. It was the order of the conversation. We had spent years walking into rooms and opening with the answer, blockchain, to a question nobody in the room had asked yet.
That day we did the opposite, almost by accident.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
We did not go there to talk about blockchain
The brief was simple: show students what AI and AI agents make possible, and show them where infrastructure fits once they start building something real.
So we started where they already were. AI can generate an application, automate a process, hold a conversation with a user. An agent can take that further and act on its own. Fine. Then you try to ship it, and a different class of problem shows up: how does this thing handle a payment? How does it touch a digital asset? How does an agent execute a transaction without a developer wiring every component from scratch?
That is the moment Avalanche entered the conversation as an answer to a question the room had arrived at on its own.
When you lead with the chain, you are asking people to care about your infrastructure. When you lead with what they are building, they ask you for it.
The question that stayed with me
Somewhere in those two extra hours, a student asked how technologies this complicated were already running inside companies like Toyota and FIFA, as things that work, used by people who have no idea they are using them.
Underneath that question was a better one: if the user never notices the blockchain, does the user need to understand it?
No. And that single answer should reorganize how this entire industry talks about itself.
The goal was never to turn everyone into a blockchain expert. The goal is to make the technology simple enough that someone with a good idea can use it without learning every layer underneath it. We spent a decade selling comprehension. We should have been selling irrelevance, the good kind, the kind where the complexity disappears into the product.
The most surprising questions that day were not technical at all. Several students asked whether the education they were in the middle of would still be worth anything given how fast AI is moving. 77472.subject: 💰 Siri is about to start paying for content
77472.body:
----------
######                  [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/he2t9cz)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Apple wants to pay publishers every time Siri borrows their words, the first AI company to offer paying by the use instead of a flat fee. Google halved the price of its newest model, OpenAI's revenue chief walked out days after its COO, and Amazon started training AI on Twitch streamers unless they dig into settings and switch it off.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Apple:** Why will it pay every time you ask Siri?

* **Google:** What did it just cut in half?

* **OpenAI:** Who walked out days before the IPO?

* **Amazon:** What is it taking from Twitch by default?


----------



----------
## Apple will pay the news every time Siri uses it

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e04a38b7-7cae-4206-825a-bbf56a15085f/Newsletter_14_Aug_-_1.jpg?t=1786686905)
Caption: 

Apple is [in talks to pay publishers](https://www.wsj.com/business/media/apple-in-talks-to-pay-publishers-to-improve-ai-powered-siri-0641f64b) for the content that will feed its new Siri, and the way it wants to pay is the real story. Instead of a flat licensing fee, Apple has floated paying each time Siri actually uses a publisher's work.

That pay-as-you-go model breaks the industry norm, where an AI company hands over one fixed sum for broad access to an archive. OpenAI's deal with News Corp was $250 million over five years. Apple would rather meter it.

The budget under discussion runs into nine figures, per the Wall Street Journal, and Apple has been reaching out to publishers for months.

It's a different posture from the rest of the field, which mostly trains on scraped work and settles the lawsuits later. Apple is offering to pay by the use before anyone sues.

The new Siri lands later this year. If it leans on the news as much as Apple expects, the meter starts running then.


----------







----------
## The AI profits went to people who got in early

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e26a5a49-9574-4bc5-881d-9318cfb80afd/ChatGPT_Image_Aug_7__2026__11_00_32_AM.png?t=1786089655)
Follow image link: (https://invest.genai.works/)
Caption: 

In 2019 Khosla Ventures put $50 million into OpenAI, which was then a research lab with no product and no revenue. That stake is worth billions now.
